title: Sardegna's Diesel Bill Climbs Faster Than Petrol's This Week
dek: Both fuels in Sardegna still undercut the national self-service average, but Gasolio has gained nearly three times as fast as Benzina over the last seven days.
body: Self-service drivers in Sardegna paid €2.008 for Benzina and €2.123 for Gasolio as of August 4th, both a shade below the national self-service averages of €2.012 and €2.128. The gap is small — about half a cent on petrol and under a cent on diesel — but it means the island is currently one of the more affordable places to fill up in Italy, at least at the pump price level.

The direction of travel is the more interesting story. Over the past week Sardegna's self-service Benzina rose from €1.996 to €2.008, a 0.6% increase, while Gasolio jumped from €2.088 to €2.123, up 1.6% — nearly triple the pace. Behind those prices, the region's station network stayed active: 677 stations are registered on the island and 613 of them reported prices on the 4th, a 90% reporting rate that shows the local network is still being closely tracked day to day.

Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Sardegna, where self-service diesel has climbed 1.6% in just a week — almost triple the pace of petrol — even though both fuels still sit a touch below Italy's national average.
